text: Which platform was GSE309890 run on, and what organism is it?

## Abstract
The GEO Series GSE309890 ran on platform GPL24659, which corresponds to Escherichia coli str. K-12 substr. MG1655. This study explored the metabolic effects of sertraline in antibiotic resistance emergence using high-throughput sequencing techniques. GSE309890 includes six samples and presents an unpublished study as of yet.

## I. Introduction
**Background:** 
The study aimed to understand how the SSRI sertraline impacts antibiotic resistance emergence in Escherichia coli through metabolic changes in the pentose phosphate pathway.

**Literature Review:** 
No PubMed record is linked to this GEO study, indicating either an unpublished or not indexed study.

**Knowledge Gap:** 
While SSRI effects on antibiotic resistance have been suggested, the metabolic shift's role remained unexplored before this study's experiment.

**Objective & Hypothesis:** 
Objective was to evaluate adaptive resistance in E. coli under stress induced by sertraline. Hypothesis: Sertraline-driven redox modulation enhances resistance emergence.

## II. Materials and Methods
**Study Design:** 
No new experimental data obtained; records aim was metadata insights.
